channel.description: WSJ World News RSS, without Opinions

item.title: Middle East Oil Exports Rebound as Iran’s Chokehold on Hormuz Breaks Down
item.description: The erosion of Iran’s position comes as the U.S. Navy and Gulf oil producers have become better at fending off or evading Iranian attacks, allowing more tankers to cross the strait.

item.title: Raytheon Gets $20.7 Billion Contract to Accelerate AMRAAM Missile Production
item.description: Under the five-year contract, with two option years, Raytheon said it will scale AMRAAM missile production to record levels to meet long-term demand.

item.title: Software Glitch Will Delay Approval of Boeing’s Latest 737 MAX Model
item.description: Plus, British counterterrorism police release suspects in terror plot at base hosting U.S. forces and Trump unveils $15 billion Iowa steel project.

item.title: The Small English Town Rattled by Alleged Terror Plot Near U.S. Bomber Base
item.description: Locals in Fairford question whether it really was a terror plot or something more mundane.

item.title: U.K. Releases Suspects in Terror Plot at Base Hosting U.S. Forces
item.description: Investigators said they were probing whether Iran or an Islamist group had orchestrated the plot, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Saudi Arabia Resumes Red Sea Oil Exports in Blow to Iran
item.description: Saudi Aramco is currently operating the pipeline at a throughput rate of around 3.5 million barrels a day, people familiar with the matter said.

item.title: Oil Prices Pare Gains After Saudi Pipeline Reopens
item.description: Oil prices trimmed earlier gains as Saudi Arabia’s state supplier reopened a key distribution point.

item.title: Senate Investigation Finds Rampant Use of Tether’s Stablecoin by Iranian Regime
item.description: Wallets sanctioned over Iran ties overwhelmingly dealt in Tether’s USDT stablecoin, according to Senate Democrats.

item.title: Egypt Warned Netanyahu of Impending Attack on Israel Before Oct. 7
item.description: The alert adds to claims that the Israeli leader ignored signs of Hamas’s battle plans, giving his election opponents fuel.

item.title: A Secretive North Korean POW Handover Becomes Public—and Controversial
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky divulged the current location of two captured soldiers, irking South Korea who thought such disclosures were off-limits.

item.title: How Evan Gershkovich Kept Reporting From Inside Russia’s Prison System
item.description: The reporter sits down with WSJ Editor in Chief Emma Tucker to discuss his arrest and imprisonment in Moscow’s infamous Lefortovo prison.

item.title: Best High-Yield Savings Accounts for September 2026: Up to 4.50%
item.description: These are the accounts that offer the best interest rates—without burdensome fees, gimmicks or other hassles

item.title: The Morning Risk Report: U.S. Appeals Court Upholds Pentagon Labeling Anthropic a Security Risk
item.description: Plus: AI a nightmare for regulators and U.S. defense firms push to build missile output is coming too late.

item.title: BOE’s Ramsden Sees Case for Raising Key Rate if Inflationary Pressures Build
item.description: The rise in government bond yields will help limit the impact of higher energy costs on U.K. prices, but the Bank of England may have to raise its key interest rate if inflationary pressures build, Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden said.

item.title: U.S. Pressure Is Awakening an Energy Giant in Canada
item.description: America’s trade hostility and war in the Middle East could fuel a renaissance in Canada.

item.title: In the World’s Tuna Capital, Fishermen Are Being Drawn Into a Deadly Drug War
item.description: Payouts have pulled some fishermen in the Ecuadorean city of Manta into drug trafficking, while U.S. strikes at sea have also targeted those who deny any role in the trade.

item.title: A Supermarket Opened a Pub to Get Around Liquor Laws. Now It Needs Bouncers.
item.description: The bar at Lidl’s new store in Northern Ireland is more than a marketing stunt, even if it has seating that resembles shopping carts.

item.title: Looking at Europe’s Glass as Half-Full
item.description: A narrow focus on Europe’s problems without acknowledging its strengths is making businesses wary, pushing households to build savings and putting Europe’s economic future at risk, according to ING’s chief economist.

item.title: Defense Firms Are Rushing to Boost Missile Output. It’s Coming Too Late.
item.description: Factories central to refilling America’s weapons stockpiles have suffered from underinvestment and inconsistent contracting.

item.title: U.S. Says No Plans to Sell Weapons to China After Perdue Comments
item.description: The ambassador to China said President Trump offered to sell arms to Xi Jinping.
